findings.title: Pages jump as the forecast, plan and guides arrive
findings.route_state: Today, My Home, Better Habits and Welcome, default load
findings.evidence: prod-metrics perf.cls at 390x844 / 1280x720: today 0.283 / 0.104, home 0.416 / 0.226, habits 0.284 / 0.196, welcome 0.157 / 0.075. Local fixtures: home-within 0.852 (390), 0.806 (320); today-within 0.227 (390). capture.mjs sums every layout-shift entry without recent input, not Chrome's 5 s session window, unthrottled and headless. Likely causes from code: the Loading placeholder (States.tsx:7-22, about 160 px) is swapped for the taller TodayLead and plan card. My Home's 'Today, for your home' section mounts only once the plan starts (MyHome.tsx showToday), above the guides. | verifier: prod perf.cls today 390x844 0.283, home 0.416, habits 0.284. Local today/loading cls 0 (390) and 0.02 (320) against plan-building 0.227/0.22 = within 0.227/0.22, so the Today shift comes from Loading (States.tsx:7-22, about 162 px) being swapped for TodayLead (AppShell.tsx:373-397). My Home: MyHome.tsx:50-54 showToday mounts the section above the guides. Welcome 0.157 occurs only on a direct /app/welcome load; prod app-noplace /app is 0 at 390. Plan replies were replayed (plan.replayed 13), so AI latency is not in these numbers.
findings.problem: Content above the reader's position grows after first paint and pushes the rest of the page down.
findings.user_impact: On phones the text being read moves, and a tap aimed at a help choice or a 'Why it matters' card can land on something else.
findings.fix: Reserve space. Give the loading placeholders a min-height close to the card each one replaces. Render My Home's 'Today, for your home' section from first paint whenever a place is set, in its building state.
findings.verify_reason: The numbers match prod-metrics perf.cls exactly: today 0.283/0.104, home 0.416/0.226, habits 0.284/0.196, welcome 0.157/0.075. Locally, home/within is 0.852 at 390 and 0.806 at 320, and today/within is 0.227. capture.mjs:217-222 adds up every layout-shift entry without recent input. Two parts of the stated cause need correcting. (1) On Today, the jump comes from the forecast arriving, not the plan card. In local today/loading (forecast held back) CLS is 0 at 390 and 0.02 at 320. In plan-building (forecast in, plan held back) it is 0.227/0.22, the same as within. (2) Welcome does not fit the cause. Prod app-noplace (/app redirects to the same Welcome page) is 0 at 390, and local welcome/noplace is 0. Only a direct load of /app/welcome shifts, and the cause there is unknown. Also, in prod the plan was replayed instantly on every load after the first (plan.realCalls 1, replayed 13), so real AI latency was never measured. The help-choice mis-tap example is at y 1562+ at 390, below the first screen. The My Home case is the strongest: MyHome.tsx:50-54 mounts 'Today, for your home' (4 cards locally, 1 in prod) above guide cards that are already on screen. Today 0.283 and Home 0.416 on phone are above the 0.25 'poor' line, so P2 holds at medium confidence.

findings.title: The 'For you' line repeats the recommendation's own advice
findings.route_state: Today top recommendation and My Home 'Today, for your home', AI plan, no household answers
findings.evidence: prod-today-default-1280x720-first.jpg, prod-today-default-768x1024-first.jpg, prod-home-default-390x844-full.jpg. The card says 'Incense, mosquito coils, candles and tobacco all add smoke indoors. Using them less, or not indoors, is the simplest indoor-air step.' 'For you' says 'Incense, mosquito coils, candles and tobacco add smoke indoors, so using them less is a simple step for your home air.' The prompt forbids repeating the advice (server/src/services/ai/prompts.ts:51), but planOutput.ts:160-165 checks only length and numbers. This is one real AI reply (plan.realCalls 1). | verifier: prompts.ts:52-53 (not :51). planOutput.ts:160-192 checks length, ids, numbers and BANNED wording, with no repetition check. prompts.ts:44-46 limits forYou to the candidate's reason and the air context. Screenshots as cited.
findings.problem: The personalised line adds nothing personal and doubles the length of the app's main answer.
findings.user_impact: The main card reads as filler, and on a phone it is about 4 lines longer than needed.
findings.fix: When the household context is empty, drop forYou on the server, since there is nothing personal to add. Optionally, also reject a forYou that mostly repeats the candidate's text in planOutput validation.
findings.verify_reason: The restatement is real. prod-today-default-768x1024-first.jpg, prod-today-default-1280x720-first.jpg and prod-home-default-390x844-full.jpg all show the card text, and below it 'For you' repeats it almost word for word (4 extra lines at 390). Two evidence details are wrong. The 'do not repeat' rule is at prompts.ts:52-53 ('Do not change, repeat or contradict the candidates' advice'), not :51. checkPlanOutput (planOutput.ts:156-195) checks length, ids, unknown numbers and banned wording, not only length and numbers; none of these checks catches repetition. prompts.ts:44-46 limits forYou to 'the candidate's reason and the air context', which pushes the model toward restating the reason. There is only one real reply (plan.realCalls 1). Dropping forYou whenever the context is empty is a product decision, because forYou may also draw on the air context. The smaller fix is a similarity check, or tightening the prompt wording, after confirming what a failed check falls back to.

findings.title: On phones, Tab goes to the bottom bar before the place chip at the top
findings.route_state: All app pages with a place (Today, Ask captured)
findings.evidence: prod-metrics keyboard today and ask at 390x844: step 2 is the logo (top 10), steps 3–7 are the nav links (top 788), step 8 is 'Change place' (top 10), then the content. The DOM order is logo, AppNav, PlaceChip (AppShell.tsx:275-289), and AppNav is fixed to the bottom below md (AppNav.tsx:42). | verifier: prod keyboard today 390x844 and ask 390x844, steps 2-8. AppShell.tsx:275-289. AppNav.tsx:42. Fix caveat: md:order-last creates a new visual/focus mismatch at md and wider.
findings.problem: Focus jumps from the top of the screen to the bottom and back up before reaching content. The order does not match what is seen (WCAG 2.4.3).
findings.user_impact: Keyboard and switch users on small screens lose track of where focus is.
findings.fix: Render PlaceChip before AppNav in the header and add md:order-last to the chip so the desktop row looks unchanged. Desktop focus would then go logo, chip, nav.
findings.verify_reason: The data holds. In prod keyboard today/ask at 390x844, step 2 is the logo (top 10), steps 3-7 are the nav (top 788) and step 8 is 'Change place' (top 10). The DOM order is logo, AppNav, PlaceChip (AppShell.tsx:275-289), and the nav is fixed to the bottom below md (AppNav.tsx:42). The WCAG 2.4.3 framing is arguable. A skip link comes first (step 1), every step has a visible, unobscured ring, and axe reports 0. Putting a bottom tab bar right after the header is a common pattern. The proposed fix moves the mismatch to desktop: with the chip first in the DOM and md:order-last, desktop focus would go logo, then chip (far right), then nav (middle). The fix should either put the chip beside the logo at every width (DOM and visual order agree), or move the phone bar after main.

findings.title: Large headings break mid-word or at the hyphen on 320 px phones
findings.route_state: Today H1 (long place) and verdict H2
findings.evidence: local-today-long-place-320x640-first.jpg: the H1 breaks 'Thiruvananthapura / m'; that line is full, so the real city name alone overflows a 288 px line at 30 px. prod-today-default-320x640-first.jpg: the verdict breaks 'India's 24- / hour limits'. Causes: body overflow-wrap: break-word (index.css) and text-3xl at every width (AppShell.tsx:355, TodayLead.tsx:37). | verifier: local-today-long-place-320x640-first.jpg (H1 mid-word break; local verdict y 491 against 347). The '24-/hour' break in prod-today-default-320x640-first.jpg is a legal hyphen break, not caused by index.css:92. The index.css:89-91 comment says break-word never fires at normal text.
findings.problem: Words in the two largest headings split in awkward places on small phones.
findings.user_impact: The place name and the main verdict are harder to read at a glance.
findings.fix: Use text-2xl below sm for the Today H1 and verdict H2. Use a non-breaking hyphen in the verdict's '24-hour', and update the e2e strings that match it.
findings.verify_reason: Only the H1 mid-word break is a defect. local-today-long-place-320x640-first.jpg shows 'Thiruvananthapura / m'. The line fills about 266 of 288 px, so the real city name alone would overflow by a few px at text-3xl (AppShell.tsx:355). That contradicts the index.css:89-91 comment that break-word 'never fires at normal text'. The verdict's 'India's 24- / hour limits' (prod-today-default-320x640-first.jpg) is the browser's normal break after a hyphen. overflow-wrap does not cause it, so it is typographic polish (a recommendation), and its non-breaking-hyphen fix edits a rule-checked verdict string and the e2e strings. The fixture's 70-character place name is invented; the real-city overflow is an inference from line width. The evidence is mixed: local for the H1, production for the verdict.

strengths: The answer comes first: on a 320x640 phone the first screen shows 'Forecast within India's 24-hour limits' (y 327) with its 'Within the limit' tag, 'Model forecast · Open-Meteo · updated 9:13 AM' and the caveat that within the limit is not clean or risk-free (prod-today-default-320x640-first.jpg).

The recommendation builds itself: one real AI plan returned 200 on load (plan.realCalls 1). 'Your recommendation for today' is on screen 2 at 320 and screen 1 at 1280, and 'Why this recommendation?' is one Tab after the place chip (keyboard today step 9).

The data-honesty rules hold across all 48 prod captures: bannedWords is empty everywhere, the Today default view shows CPCB 0 and AQI 0, and the landing states 'Forecasts are model estimates, not station measurements, and not the CPCB National AQI.' Its example screenshots are dated: 'A past screenshot of Today for Pune, 22 Nov 2026. Open the app for current values.'

Accessibility baseline: axe reports 0 WCAG 2.0–2.2 A/AA violations on every prod page at 390x844 and 1280x720, and there are no controls under 44 px (small [] everywhere). Every Tab stop has a visible ring and none is hidden by the bottom bar (visibleRing true, obscured false). A skip link comes first on app pages.
Reduced motion is respected: on Today, document.getAnimations() goes from 2 (cloud-drift, rain-fall) to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (prod-metrics motion).
There is no sideways scroll at 320, 390, 768, 1280 or 1440 on any page, nor with a 70-character place name or 200% text (edge [] in prod and local).

Pages load lean and quiet: one 148 kB script and one 47 kB self-hosted Inter font, LCP 1.04–1.71 s (unthrottled, indicative), and no console errors or failed requests on any app page. There were 0 HTTP 429s.

Security headers on /: a strict CSP (script-src 'self', object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'self'), HSTS with preload, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, nosniff and Referrer-Policy no-referrer (prod-vs-local-raw.txt).

Privacy is explained where it applies: 'Your browser asks first. Your location is rounded to about 1 km before it leaves your browser.' (Welcome). The household form says none of its questions asks about health conditions (Profile).

Safety notes sit next to every piece of AI or rule advice: 'Made with AI. General information only, not medical advice. Follow local public-health advisories.' (Today, My Home); 'Made by our rules' when the AI is not used.

Failure states stay useful and honest: a stale forecast shows 'Not current…' under the verdict. When the forecast fails, the rule-based plan still shows and names the forecast it rests on. A failed plan offers 'Try again' with the verdict still visible (local-today-stale/unavailable/plan-error).

Navigation and new pages work: a 5-item nav with aria-current, 56 px phone targets and safe-area padding. Deep links such as /app/home return 200, and unknown /app paths fall back to Welcome. My Home and Better Habits fill the earlier content gaps with 'Dust and cleaning' and 'Energy use' cards, each with 'Why it matters'.
The no-place first visit is now one short screen (1.1–1.5 screens): a question, a search box and 'Use my location' (prod-app-noplace-default-390x844-full.jpg).
not_checked: Expanded states were never captured open: 'Air quality details', 'See your full day', any 'Why?' panel. The rows saying where content moved (1.2, 1.3, 2.2, 2.3, 3.1, 3.2, 4.2, 11.2) rely on code-trace for the destination; production only proves the content left the default view.

Welcome steps 2–3 (chips, Skip, 'Remember on this device'), a remembered place on return (10.3), saved plans with a session (8.2), Save plan, Save my answers and Delete were not exercised, because each creates or uses an anonymous account in production.
Keyboard Tab walks exist only at 390x844 and 1280x720; 320x640 and 768x1024 were not walked.
Press feedback (:active), hover and tap feel cannot be seen in static screenshots; they come from code-trace only.
Real-phone checks (12.5): tap delay, notch and home-indicator safe areas, on-screen keyboard over inputs.
Screen-reader output, Windows High Contrast and forced-colours rendering were not checked.
CLS figures sum all layout-shift entries (not Chrome's session window), unthrottled and headless; the shifting elements were not attributed.
No real Ask AirAware call was made in production; Ask answers were seen only with local fixtures.

Local fixtures mix states that may not occur together in production: a stale-state plan card marked 'Important today' under a 'within' verdict, and an Ask answer saying 'above' while the footer says 'Within the limit'. These were not treated as product findings.
The audit's exact term-count method is not recorded; the comparison uses capture.mjs regexes over body.innerText.
Only one real AI daily-plan reply was captured (13 replays), so how often the 'For you' line repeats its card is not known.

findings.evidence: Today: 'Why this recommendation?' (DailyPlanSection.tsx:268). My Home and Better Habits: 'Why it matters' (MyHome.tsx:117, GuideGroups.tsx:78). Landing: 'Why?' (prod-landing-default-1280x720-full.jpg). The same card, 'Cut indoor smoke at the source', is labelled differently on Today and My Home (prod-today-default-1280x720-first.jpg, prod-home-default-1280x720-first.jpg). | verifier: Spec 04 §5 explicitly permits 'Why it matters' or 'Why?'. 02_PRODUCT_UX_REQUIREMENTS.md §2 uses 'Why it matters'. PlanCard.tsx:25 says Today's recommendation uses 'Why this recommendation?' by design. The one real inconsistency is the same Today card shown with two labels on Today and My Home.
findings.problem: The key explanation pattern is named inconsistently. Spec 04 §6 asks for 'the same card style and "Why?" pattern as Today'.
findings.user_impact: People may not recognise these as the same feature, and the same card looks different on two pages.
findings.fix: Use one label everywhere (for example 'Why?') and keep the screen-reader suffix with the card title.
findings.verify_reason: The three labels exist as stated (DailyPlanSection.tsx:268, MyHome.tsx:117, GuideGroups.tsx:78, PlanCard.tsx:15 default 'Why?' on Landing). They are allowed by the owner's spec, though. Spec 04 §5 says '"Why it matters" or "Why?"', and the 02 requirements table names 'Why it matters' for My Home. Spec §6 asks for the same 'pattern', which is the disclosure, not necessarily one label. PlanCard.tsx:25 documents Today's label as intended. Unifying the labels is a consistency recommendation, not a defect.

findings.title: The save note says 'Saved on this browser only', but saving creates an anonymous account on the server
findings.route_state: /app/profile 'Save my answers'; Today 'See your full day' Save plan
findings.evidence: prod-profile-default-1280x720-full.jpg and prod-profile-default-390x844-full.jpg: 'Saved on this browser only. Clearing your browser data or switching devices loses it.' appears above 'Save my answers'. This is SAVE_NOTE in HouseholdPreferencesForm.tsx:28-29, reused for Save plan in DailyPlanSection.tsx:296. The Privacy page (prod-privacy-default-1280x720-full.jpg) says that only after you press 'Save my answers' or 'Save plan' does Supabase store data in its South Asia (Mumbai) region, including an anonymous account. Welcome's 'Remember on this device' says 'Creates an anonymous save on this device' (Welcome.tsx:299-303).
findings.problem: At the moment of saving, nothing says an account is created or that answers leave the device. 'Saved on this browser only' suggests the opposite. Checklist items: 'Save … actions explain consequences' and 'No silent account creation'. Spec 04 §7 says the same.
findings.user_impact: People consent to saving with an inaccurate picture of where their household answers go.
findings.fix: Copy change only. Reword SAVE_NOTE to say that saving creates an anonymous account with no email or name, that answers are stored on AirAware's database host, that only this browser can open them, and that clearing browser data loses access. Link to /privacy. A privacy reviewer may rate this higher.
findings.verify_reason: prod-profile-default-1280x720-full.jpg shows 'Saved on this browser only. Clearing your browser data or switching devices loses it.' above 'Save my answers' (SAVE_NOTE, HouseholdPreferencesForm.tsx:28-29, reused at DailyPlanSection.tsx:296). The phrase was written as a claim about access (phase-6 design spec line 64). At the point of consent, though, it reads as a claim about storage, while Privacy.tsx:73-77 and USER_GUIDE.md:79 say saving creates an anonymous account stored in Supabase's Mumbai region. That fails the checklist item 'Save … actions explain consequences' and spec 04 §7 'explain its consequences before the user commits'. UX_AUDIT P7 already flagged 'saving quietly creates an anonymous account'. P2 is fair: the privacy page itself is accurate, so this is misleading microcopy, not a broken promise. The fix is incomplete, though. The success strings 'Saved on this browser.' (HouseholdPreferencesForm.tsx:31) and 'Saved on this browser. This is the plan as saved.' (DailyPlanSection.tsx:38) carry the same framing and need the same rewording, and e2e/journey.spec.ts:20 asserts the latter.

strengths: Today answers question 1 (the verdict) on the first screen at all five widths. It answers questions 1 to 3, including 'Why this recommendation?', at 768x1024 (firstWhy 781), 1280x720 (recommendationHeading 234, firstWhy 536) and 1440x900.

The verdict is in plain words and leads the page. Numbers live in a collapsed 'Air quality details'. On Today, m.terms has PM2.5 0, µg/m³ 0, AQI 0 and CPCB 0. The 'Model forecast · Open-Meteo · updated 9:13 AM' line and the caveat sit right under the verdict.

The recommendation builds automatically and shows one top card with Why, plus 'See your full day'. The source line ('Made with AI') and the general-information note stay visible. This fixes UX_AUDIT P2 ('8 phone screens down').

findings.title: Save and Remember text says data stays "on this browser" when it is stored on AirAware's Supabase server
findings.route_state: /app/profile (Save my answers); Today and My Home full day (Save plan); /app/welcome step 3 (Remember on this device)
findings.evidence: client/src/features/daily-plan/HouseholdPreferencesForm.tsx:28-31 (SAVE_NOTE: "Saved on this browser only. Clearing your browser data or switching devices loses it."; SAVED: "Saved on this browser."). client/src/features/daily-plan/DailyPlanSection.tsx:38 ("Saved on this browser. This is the plan as saved."). client/src/pages/Welcome.tsx:299-305 ("Creates an anonymous save on this device."). The data is actually written to the Supabase tables household_preferences and daily_plans (server/src/services/saved/supabaseStore.ts:104-105). PRIVACY.md:35 says it is stored "in Supabase (Postgres, South Asia (Mumbai) region)", and PRIVACY.md:47-48 says the owner and Supabase can read it and that clearing browser data "does not delete the rows". client/src/pages/Privacy.tsx:75 and :90 say the same. The note is visible in production: prod-profile-default-390x844-full.jpg. The wording comes from docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-18-phase6-saved-data-design.md:64, which lets the builder adjust it.
findings.problem: The text next to every save control, and the Remember hint, says the household answers and plans are kept in the browser or on the device. They are sent to and stored in AirAware's server-side database. That text also implies clearing browser data removes the data, but the rows stay until "Delete my saved data" or the idle-account cleanup.
findings.user_impact: A person deciding whether to save sensitive household details (children, older adults, someone more sensitive, cooking fuel) is told they stay on their own browser. They agree on that basis, but the data leaves the device and can be read by the project owner and the host. Someone who clears their browser to remove it leaves it on the server.
findings.fix: Reword the three strings to match PRIVACY.md. For example, the note: "Saved to an anonymous AirAware account that only this browser can open. Clearing browser data loses access but does not delete it; use Delete my saved data." The Welcome hint: "Saves your answers and searched place to an anonymous account linked to this browser." Update the phase-6 spec string with them.
findings.verify_reason: Every claim checks out. HouseholdPreferencesForm.tsx:28-31 has SAVE_NOTE 'Saved on this browser only. findings.verify_reason: The code path is real. airCheck.ts:23-34 windows on each request's own UTC hour. cachedForecast.ts:4 caches for 10 minutes per process. dailyPlan.ts:150-156 fetches and assesses separately.
